Place value.title: Hundreds, tens and ones
Place value.body: Every digit has a place. In 438, the 4 is in the hundreds place (400), the 3 is in the tens place (30) and the 8 is in the ones place (8). So 438 = 400 + 30 + 8.

Place value.title: Reading and writing numbers
Place value.body: We say 438 as 'four hundred thirty-eight'. A zero holds a place: in 405 there are 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones.

Place value.question: In the number 726, what is the value of the digit 2?
Place value.explanation: The 2 is in the tens place, so its value is 2 tens = 20.

Addition.title: Add place by place
Addition.body: Line up the numbers so ones sit under ones, tens under tens and hundreds under hundreds. Add the ones first, then the tens, then the hundreds.

Addition.title: Regrouping (carrying)
Addition.body: If a column adds up to 10 or more, regroup. In 276 + 148, the ones are 6 + 8 = 14. Write 4 and carry 1 ten. Tens: 7 + 4 + 1 = 12, so write 2 and carry 1 hundred. Hundreds: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. The answer is 424.

Subtraction.title: Subtract place by place
Subtraction.body: Start with the ones, then the tens, then the hundreds. Always subtract the bottom number from the top number.

Subtraction.title: Regrouping (borrowing)
Subtraction.body: If the top digit is smaller, borrow 1 from the next place. In 432 - 178, you cannot take 8 from 2, so borrow a ten: 12 - 8 = 4. Tens: 2 - 7 does not work, so borrow a hundred: 12 - 7 = 5. Hundreds: 3 - 1 = 2. The answer is 254.

Subtraction.question: What is 503 - 247?
Subtraction.explanation: Borrow across the zero: 503 - 247 = 256. Check by adding: 256 + 247 = 503.

Multiplication.title: Equal groups
Multiplication.body: Multiplication is a quick way to add equal groups. 4 bags with 6 apples each is 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24, written 4 × 6 = 24.

Multiplication.title: Arrays and patterns
Multiplication.body: An array puts objects in rows and columns. 3 rows of 5 make 3 × 5 = 15. Order does not matter: 3 × 5 = 5 × 3. Skip counting helps: count by 5s three times, 5, 10, 15.

Multiplication.question: A box has 5 rows of 4 mangoes. How many mangoes are there?

Division.title: Sharing equally
Division.body: Division splits a number into equal groups. 12 candies shared by 3 friends gives 4 each, written 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

Division.title: Multiplication and division are partners
Division.body: Because 4 × 3 = 12, we know 12 ÷ 3 = 4 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Use multiplication facts to check division answers.

Fractions.title: Parts of a whole
Fractions.body: A fraction names equal parts of a whole. If a pizza is cut into 4 equal slices and you eat 1, you ate 1/4. The bottom number (denominator) tells how many equal parts. The top number (numerator) tells how many you have.

Fractions.title: Comparing fractions
Fractions.body: When the numerators are the same, the fraction with the smaller denominator is bigger, because its pieces are larger. So 1/2 > 1/3 > 1/4. On a number line, 1/2 sits halfway between 0 and 1.

Fractions.question: Which fraction is the smallest?
Fractions.explanation: Cutting a whole into 8 pieces makes the smallest pieces, so 1/8 is the smallest.

Measurement and data.title: Reading a clock
Measurement and data.body: The short hand shows the hour and the long hand shows the minutes. When the long hand is on 6, it is 30 minutes past. Count by 5s around the clock face to read minutes.

Measurement and data.title: Measuring length
Measurement and data.body: Line the zero of the ruler up with the start of the object and read where it ends. Short lengths use centimeters (cm). Longer ones use meters (m). 100 cm = 1 m.

Measurement and data.question: The short hand is just past 3 and the long hand points to 6. What time is it?
Measurement and data.explanation: Long hand on 6 means 30 minutes. Short hand past 3 means the hour is 3. So it is 3:30.

Geometry.title: Perimeter
Geometry.body: Perimeter is the distance around a shape. Add the lengths of all its sides. A rectangle 5 cm long and 3 cm wide has perimeter 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 cm.

Geometry.title: Area
Geometry.body: Area is the space inside a shape, counted in square units. A rectangle 4 units long and 3 units wide covers 4 × 3 = 12 square units.

Geometry.question: A square has sides of 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
Geometry.explanation: A square has 4 equal sides: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24 cm.
